q-352254.name: Question 1
q-352254.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-4+5x-{x}^{2} & =0 \\ (x-1)(x-4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=1$ and $x=4.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=1$ to $x=4.$  

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{4}x(-4+5x-{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{4}(-4x+5{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {(-2{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4})|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =2\pi ((-2({4}^{2})+\frac{5}{3}({4}^{3})-\frac{1}{4}({4}^{4}))-(-2+\frac{5}{3}-\frac{1}{4})) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{45}{4}) \\  & =\frac{45\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=2{x}^{3}-{x}^{4}$ and the $x$-axis, shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
q-139184.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{3}-{x}^{4} & =0 \\ {x}^{4}-2{x}^{3} & =0 \\ {x}^{3}(2-x) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=2.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x(2{x}^{3}-{x}^{4})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(2{x}^{4}-{x}^{5})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the finite region bounded by the curve y=2x2−x3 and the x-axis, shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated 2π radians about the y-axis?

a
2π∫02(2x2−x4)dx
b
2π∫02(−2x3+x4)2dx
c
2π∫02(2x3−x4)dx
d
2π∫02(x3−2x4)dx
e
π∫02(2x3−x4)dx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the x-axis by solving the following equation for x:

2x2−x3=0x2(2−x)=0

The solutions are x=0 and x=2. So, we need to integrate from x=0 to x=2.

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

V=2π∫abxf(x)dx=2π∫02x(2x2−x3)dx=2π∫02(2x3−x4)dx

q-352258.name: Question 5
q-352258.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-6+5x-{x}^{2} & =0 \\ (x-2)(x-3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=2$ and $x=3.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=2$ to $x=3.$  

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{2}^{3}x(-6+5x-{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{2}^{3}(-6x+5{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {(-3{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4})|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =2\pi [(-3(3)^{2}+\frac{5(3)^{3}}{3}-\frac{{3}^{4}}{4})-(-3(2)^{2}+\frac{5(2)^{3}}{3}-\frac{{2}^{4}}{4})] \\  & =2\pi (\frac{5}{12}) \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

q-139295.name: Question 6
q-139295.problem: Consider the finite region bounded between the curves $y=2x$ and $y={x}^{2}-3x.$ Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
q-139295.worked_solution:
First, let $f(x)=2x$ and $g(x)={x}^{2}-3x.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ 2x & ={x}^{2}-3x \\ {x}^{2}-5x & =0 \\ x(x-5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=5.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=5.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/d8833c0c6f1becdbe2841f11fae25bb8e558edd06abee6668b2593c4e37c747b.png)

  

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=g(x)={x}^{2}-3x,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=f(x)=2x.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{5}x([2x]-[{x}^{2}-3x])\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{5}x(5x-{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{5}(5{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {(\frac{5{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})|}_{0}^{5} \\  & =2\pi [(\frac{{5}^{4}}{3}-\frac{{5}^{4}}{4})-0] \\  & =\frac{625\pi }{6}\end{aligned}

q-139282.problem: Consider the finite region bounded between the curves $y=2x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}$ and $y=-x+\frac{5}{2}.$ Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
q-139282.worked_solution:
First, let $f(x)=2x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}$ and $g(x)=-x+\frac{5}{2}.$ 

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ 2x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2} & =-x+\frac{5}{2} \\ {x}^{2}-6x+5 & =0 \\ (x-1)(x-5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=1$ and $x=5.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=1$ to $x=5.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/27919b5cbe7c0d8b7f7c58a9378f5aa3d30e5466c63b1b17d8a1b6af028ecf66.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=g(x)=-x+\frac{5}{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=f(x)=2x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{5}x([2x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]-[-x+\frac{5}{2}])\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{5}x(-{x}^{2}+6x-5)\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{5}(-{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}-5x)\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {(-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+2{x}^{3}-\frac{5{x}^{2}}{2})|}_{1}^{5} \\  & =\pi [(-\frac{625}{4}+250-\frac{125}{2})-(-\frac{1}{4}+2-\frac{5}{2})] \\  & =\pi [\frac{125}{4}-(-\frac{3}{4})] \\  & =32\pi \end{aligned}
$$

First, let $f(x)=x$ and $g(x)=\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ x & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{4} \\ 4x-{x}^{3} & =0 \\ x(4-{x}^{2}) & =0 \\ x(2-x)(2+x) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0,$ $x=-2,$ and $x=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=2$ because we are only concerned about $x\ge 0.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/ccbaa663f6f108322f7bafd4a192a5b9acdf913b61b8319048e92b7885458a91.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=g(x)=\frac{{x}^{3}}{4},$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=f(x)=x.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x([x]-[\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}])\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x(x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{4})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(4{x}^{2}-{x}^{4})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves y=x and y=x34, as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated 2π radians about the y-axis.

a
2π∫02(x4−4x2)dx
b
π∫02(x4−x2)dx
c
π2∫02(4x4−x2)dx
d
2π∫02(x4−x2)dx
e
π2∫02(4x2−x4)dx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let f(x)=x and g(x)=x34.

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for x:

f(x)=g(x)x=x344x−x3=0x(4−x2)=0x(2−x)(2+x)=0

The solutions are x=0, x=−2, and x=2. So, we need to integrate from x=0 to x=2 because we are only concerned about x≥0.

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

The vertical arrow

  • enters the region through the lower function y=g(x)=x34, and

  • leaves through the upper function y=f(x)=x.

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

V=2π∫abx([upper]−[lower])dx=2π∫02x([x]−[x34])dx=2π∫02x(x−x34)dx=π2∫02(4x2−x4)dx

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/11b85e35604a0350a9fd7754dfda481000debb20397d9aa593a1b887409a97c7.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $y=4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}$ and $y=2x,$ as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
q-139260.worked_solution:
First, let $f(x)=4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}$ and $g(x)=2x.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ 4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2} & =2x \\ 8x-{x}^{3}-2x & =0 \\ 4x-{x}^{3} & =0 \\ x(4-{x}^{2}) & =0 \\ x(2-x)(2+x)\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-2,$ $x=0,$ and $x=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=2$ because we are only concerned about $x\ge 0.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/e03c88c1d24116cc9f68c69150eba39cb6593b4bf6fd4ca9640987ce4ba62299.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=g(x)=2x,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=f(x)=4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x([4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}]-[2x])\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x(2x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(2{x}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves y=4x−x32 and y=2x, as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated 2π radians about the y-axis.

a
2π∫02(2x2−x42)dx
b
2π∫02(2x−x4)2dx
c
2π∫02(2x2−x4)dx
d
π2∫02(2x2−x4)dx
e
π2∫02(x2−x42)dx
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let f(x)=4x−x32 and g(x)=2x.

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for x:

f(x)=g(x)4x−x32=2x8x−x3−2x=04x−x3=0x(4−x2)=0x(2−x)(2+x)

The solutions are x=−2, x=0, and x=2. So, we need to integrate from x=0 to x=2 because we are only concerned about x≥0.

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

The vertical arrow

  • enters the region through the lower function y=g(x)=2x, and

  • leaves through the upper function y=f(x)=4x−x32.

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

V=2π∫abx([upper]−[lower])dx=2π∫02x([4x−x32]−[2x])dx=2π∫02x(2x−x32)dx=2π∫02(2x2−x42)dx

q-352642.worked_solution:
First, let $f(x)=\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x$ and $g(x)=-{x}^{3}+\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ \frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x & =-{x}^{3}+\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x \\ 3{x}^{2}+5x & =-2{x}^{3}+7{x}^{2}+5x \\ 2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2} & =0 \\ 2{x}^{2}(x-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=2.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/d19b70836b7b377c498fa505868563115706b588b0a2216d09c6ec738f746bbd.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=f(x)=\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=g(x)=-{x}^{3}+\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x([-{x}^{3}+\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x]-[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}x])\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x(-{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(-{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {(-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{2})|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2\pi [(-\frac{{2}^{5}}{5}+\frac{{2}^{4}}{2})-0] \\  & =2\pi (-\frac{32}{5}+8) \\  & =2\pi \cdot \frac{8}{5} \\  & =\frac{16\pi }{5}\end{aligned}
$$
